- Commercial: likely low-tier monthly commit if host supports predictable burst for 1–2 peaks/day.
- Positive: likes pricing transparency and quickstart docs; downside: wants clearer docs on quotas and guidance for self-serve defaults.
- SE notes: propose trial config with 100 concurrent requests cap, route-level quota for webhooks, and recommend local leaky-bucket queue in front of API.
- Marketing/ops ask: add example SDK code for backoff + token bucket; provide sample dashboard queries to surface 429s and concurrency anomalies.

use_case_summary: TiltBay is building an AI-first support assistant + KB search for small merchants. They expect unpredictable daily traffic spikes after marketing pushes and batch imports. Need hosted API (self-serve) with clear rate-limits, per-key concurrency control, and recommendations for burst handling and retry semantics. Primary goals: minimize customer-visible 429s, keep latency <300ms for chat median, and cap monthly cost under their SMB budget.
technical_requirements:
- Per-key and per-route concurrency limits
- Burst allowance for short spikes (2–10 minutes)
- Clear 429 semantics and headers to surface remaining quota
- SDK examples for exponential backoff + jitter + retry-after handling
- Support for streaming responses for live chat
- Admin console to view token consumption by API key
sales_notes:
- Upsell opportunity: burst add-on or small dedicated pool if spikes become regular.
- Pricing sensitivity: will negotiate small monthly commit (~$1k–$5k ARR range) if burst behavior is guaranteed.
- Close plan: technical success metrics -> procurement approval -> convert to paid monthly plan
recommended_poC_config: 1) Staging keys with per-key limit 100 concurrent; 2) Route-level quota for webhooks set to 200 requests/min with leaky-bucket smoothing; 3) Client SDK changes to implement backoff with randomized jitter; 4) Monitor 429 rate and 95th latency for 48h
